arxiv-2101-00928.title: Search for new physics via baryon EDM at LHC
arxiv-2101-00928.creator: L. Henry 1, D. Marangotto 2, A. Merli 2,3, N. Neri 2,3, J. Ruiz 1, F. Martinez Vidal 1
arxiv-2101-00928.description: Abstract Permanent electric dipole moments (EDMs) of fundamental particles provide powerful probes for physics beyond the Standard Model. We propose to search for the EDM of strange and charm baryons at LHC, extending the ongoing experimental program on the neutron, muon, atoms, molecules and light nuclei.

arxiv-2301-04939.title: Safe Policy Improvement for POMDPs via Finite-State Controllers
arxiv-2301-04939.creator: Thiago D. Simão, Marnix Suilen, Nils Jansen
arxiv-2301-04939.description: Abstract We study safe policy improvement (SPI) for partially observable Markov decision processes (POMDPs). SPI is an offline reinforcement learning (RL) problem that assumes access to (1) historical data about an environment, and (2) the so-called behavior policy that previously generated this data by interacting with the environment.

arxiv-2307-14550.title: Irreversible evolution, obstacles in fitness landscapes and persistent drug resistance
arxiv-2307-14550.creator: Kristina Crona
arxiv-2307-14550.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Kristina Crona. We use fitness graphs, or directed cube graphs, for analyzing evolutionary reversibility. The main application is antimicrobial drug resistance. Reversible drug resistance has been observed both clinically and experimentally. If drug resistance depends on a single point mutation, then a possible scenario is that the mutation reverts back to the wild-type codon after the drug has been discontinued, so that susceptibility is fully restored. In general, a drug pause does not automatically imply fast elimination of drug resistance.

arxiv-2410-18481.title: Dialog2Flow: Pre-training Soft-Contrastive Action-Driven Sentence Embeddings for Automatic Dialog Flow Extraction
arxiv-2410-18481.creator: Sergio Burdisso, Srikanth Madikeri, Petr Motlicek
arxiv-2410-18481.description: Abstract Efficiently deriving structured workflows from unannotated dialogs remains an underexplored and formidable challenge in computational linguistics. Automating this process could significantly accelerate the manual design of workflows in new domains and enable the grounding of large language models in domain-specific flowcharts, enhancing transparency and controllability.

arxiv-2503-09316.title: Exploring Coronal Abundances of M Dwarfs at Moderate Activity Level
arxiv-2503-09316.creator: J. J. Chebly, K. Poppenhäger, J. D. Alvarado-Gómez, B. E . Wood
arxiv-2503-09316.description: Abstract Context. Main sequence stars of spectral types F, G, and K with low to moderate activity levels exhibit a recognizable pattern known as the first ionization potential effect (FIP effect), where elements with lower first ionization potentials are more abundant in the stellar corona than in the photosphere.

arxiv-2509-03705.title: Cavity-Controlled High Harmonic Generation
arxiv-2509-03705.creator: Zohar Amitay, Nimrod Moiseyev
arxiv-2509-03705.description: Abstract Employing non-Hermitian Floquet theory, the strong-field process of high harmonic (HH) generation by a classical continuous-wave field irradiating ground-state atom is discovered to be controllable by placing the irradiated atom inside a single-mode quantum cavity initiated even with a single photon.

pmc-10871168.title: Genomic epidemiology reveals the dominance of Hennepin County in the transmission of SARS-CoV-2 in Minnesota from 2020 to 2022
pmc-10871168.creator: Matthew Scotch, Kimberly Lauer, Eric D. Wieben, Yesesri Cherukuri, Julie M. Cunningham, Eric W. Klee, Jonathan J. Harrington, Julie S. Lau, Samantha J. McDonough, Mark Mutawe, John C. O'Horo, Chad E. Rentmeester, Nicole R. Schlicher, Valerie T. White, Susan K. Schneider, Peter T. Vedell, Xiong Wang,
pmc-10871168.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) has had an unprecedented impact on human health and highlights the need for genomic epidemiology studies to increase our understanding of virus evolution and spread and to inform policy decisions. We sequenced viral genomes from over 22,000 patient samples tested at Mayo Clinic Laboratories between 2020 and 2022 and used Bayesian phylodynamics to describe county and regional spread in Minnesota.

pmc-10898891.title: Cancer care in Lebanon and the climate-proofing of a burning phoenix
pmc-10898891.creator: Mohamad Ibrahim
pmc-10898891.description: Beirut, the capital of Lebanon, has been burnt and rebuilt seven times, earning the title of an urban phoenix. Its strategic geolocation in the heart of the Mediterranean gave the country leverage for the economy, by becoming a hotspot for trade through its different ports.

pmc-11395755.title: Constructing condylar cartilage organoid to explore primary cilia functions
pmc-11395755.creator: Zhan Liu, Haoyu Zhou, Qingwei Wu, Tianhao Luo, Hanlin Tu, Guoliang Sa, Xuewen Yang
pmc-11395755.description: An organoid culture system better recapitulates the cellular structure, function, and interaction between cells and the extracellular matrix (ECM) than a two-dimensional (2D) culture system. We here constructed a condylar cartilage organoid to explore the regulatory role of primary cilia. Similar to the natural condylar cartilage, the condylar cartilage organoid exhibited abundant ECM and comprised superficial, proliferative, and hypertrophic zones.

pmc-11438838.title: Optimal directed acyclic graph federated learning model for energy-efficient IoT communication networks
pmc-11438838.creator: G Nalinipriya, E Laxmi Lydia, S Rama Sree, Denis Nikolenko, Sirisha Potluri, Janjhyam Venkata Naga Ramesh, Sheela Jayachandran
pmc-11438838.description: Federated learning (FL) stimulates distributed on-device computation systems to process an optimum technique efficiency by communicating local process upgrades and global method distribution from aggregation averaging procedure. On-device FL is a standard application in wireless environments, with several mobile devices participating as nodes in the FL network.

pmc-12614406.creator: Hannah M Wedig, Charles T Talbot, Marc R Raffe, Manuel Boller, Melissa Edwards, Kristin M Zersen, Kelly E Hall
pmc-12614406.description: ObjectiveTo report summative data from the American College of Veterinary Emergency and Critical Care Veterinary Committee on Trauma (ACVECC‐VetCOT) registry, with further summary reporting based on geographic region and human population density.DesignMulti‐institutional registry data report, January 1, 2022 to December 31, 2023.SettingTwenty‐two Veterinary Trauma Centers (VTCs) identified and verified by ACVECC‐VetCOT.

pmc-13296980.title: Prefrontal Oxygenation During Exercise and Inhibitory Control After Aerobic and Game-Based Exercise in Young Adults
pmc-13296980.creator: Youmin Son, Yeonhak Jung
pmc-13296980.description: Highlights What are the main findings? Greater global prefrontal oxy-Hb during exercise was associated with greater subsequent improvement in inhibitory control, indexed by reduced Flanker cost.Game-based exercise elicited higher prefrontal oxy-Hb during exercise than aerobic exercise, but Flanker cost improvement did not differ significantly between conditions. What are the implications of the main findings?

pmc-13348081.title: A retrospective review of leprosy diagnosed histopathologically from skin biopsy specimens in central South Africa
pmc-13348081.creator: Ruben B. van Wyk, Danita L. le Grange, Liska Budding
pmc-13348081.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundLeprosy, caused by Mycobacterium leprae, remains a condition designated by the World Health Organization (WHO) as a neglected tropical disease, despite formal eradication in South Africa. Histopathology is pivotal in the diagnosis of leprosy, particularly in resource-limited settings.ObjectivesThe study aimed to describe the histopathological spectrum and clinical features of leprosy diagnosed on skin biopsies over a 10-year period in central South Africa.MethodA retrospective review was performed of histologically confirmed leprosy cases diagnosed from January 2015 to December 2024.

pmc-13375885.title: Inducing tumor-intrinsic innate immune response to break cancer immunotherapy resistance
pmc-13375885.creator: Jessica A. Blandino, Takahiko Murayama
pmc-13375885.description: Immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) therapy targeting the PD-1/PD-L1 axis has dramatically transformed cancer treatment. However, durable responses are limited to a subset of patients, particularly for those with solid tumors. Therefore, understanding the resistance mechanisms and developing a novel therapeutic strategy are urgent priorities.

pmc-13468590.title: Design, Synthesis, In Silico and In Vitro Pharmacological Profiling of Cannabidiol-like Synthetic Analogues as Multi-Target Anti-Alzheimer’s Agents
pmc-13468590.creator: Boris P. Stoyanov, Borislav Georgiev, Denitsa Stefanova, Virginia Tzankova, Elena Kalcheva-Yovkova, Nikolay Vassilev, Miroslav Rangelov, Nadezhda Todorova, Dimitrina Zheleva-Dimitrova, Boris Shivachev, Violina T. Angelova
pmc-13468590.description: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a multifactorial neurodegenerative disorder that requires therapeutic agents capable of targeting multiple pathological pathways. In this study, a series of cannabidiol (CBD)-like hydrazone derivatives (3a–i) was synthesized and characterized by NMR, HRMS, and single-crystal X-ray diffraction for compound 3i.

pmc-13485735.title: ADORA2A activation restores lysosomal function and photoreceptor outer segment degradation in stressed retinal pigment epithelium
pmc-13485735.creator: Daodian Tao, Daiying Zhou, Mingjuan Wu, Peiling Xie, Yunhao Zhang, Jing Bao
pmc-13485735.description: BackgroundAge-related macular degeneration (AMD) involves early retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) dysfunction and impaired processing of photoreceptor outer segments (POS). We investigated whether ADORA2A regulates post-ingestive POS handling and lysosomal recovery under AMD-relevant stress.MethodsA2E-stressed ARPE-19 cells, primary porcine RPE cells, and a sodium iodate-induced mouse model were studied. ADORA2A was activated with CGS21680 and inhibited with ZM241385.

pmc-13525907.title: The cold‐water immersion recovery–adaptation paradox: Reconciling acute parasympathetic and analgesic benefits with chronic hypertrophy attenuation
pmc-13525907.creator: Jose Francisco Tornero‐Aguilera, Jose Lozano‐Meca, Miguel López‐Moreno, Edgar Simón Sancho‐Haro, Mario Muñoz‐López, Eneko Baz‐Valle, José Francisco López‐Gil, Rodrigo Yáñez‐Sepúlveda, Vicente Javier Clemente‐Suárez
pmc-13525907.description: Cold‐water immersion (CWI) is among the most widely used post‐exercise recovery modalities in elite sport and clinical rehabilitation, yet a fundamental paradox now emerges from the evidence: the same protocols that accelerate parasympathetic reactivation and reduce perceived muscle soreness also suppress the molecular and cellular machinery of skeletal‐muscle hypertrophy when applied repeatedly across resistance‐training mesocycles.
